text:
Marisa: Quick sync- lease-swap sims found lost-in-flight writes when owner flips mid-request. Proposal: proxy escrow + delegate-forward model so proxy persists short-lived escrow and replays to eventual owner. Reactions?

alex: Sounds sensible. Main cost = tail latency and small storage. How do we avoid duplicates and preserve order?

marisa: Use write_token + shard_seq. At replay target does idempotent apply based on token and seq windows.

devon: Residency is the blocker- EU-only tenants must never be forwarded out. Escrow must carry residency_policy and enforce it.

marisa: Agreed. If no permitted region, mark escrow QUARANTINED and surface to ops.

sam: Is escrow durable enough? If proxy dies during outage we could lose writes.

marisa: Keep escrow replicated to two local proxies (sync) and replicate metadata to control plane for visibility. TTLs short (default 180s).

nina: Observability: add escrow_count, forward_latency_p95, quarantined_count and per-tenant traces.

marisa: Client contract: default 202 + write_token. Background forwarder handles apply. Optional sync=true for callers needing strong commit.

alex: Rollout plan?

marisa: Feature-flagged proxy -> dark launch metrics -> canary for non-sovereign tenants -> EU after legal signoff. Gate by stability and backlog.

ops-bot: [automation] defaults: escrow_replication=2; ttl_secs=180; forward_retry_limit=5; quarantine_retention_days=7.

devon: I'll draft operator runbook and failure-mode matrix.

marisa: I'll write a short RFC patch with token format, handoff handshake, and sample snippet. Example handshake:

POST /handoff
{ "write_token": "wt-123", "shard": "s-7", "seq_span": [400,402], "residency": "eu" }

marisa: Thanks all, tagging @alex @devon @sam @nina. Prototype in staging once RFC lands.
